TO: The University of Rhode Island Board of Trustees, Finance and Facilities Committee FROM: Marc B.
Parlange, Ph.D., P.Eng., President DATE: September 14, 2026 SUBJECT: Discussion: Update on URI Workday Implementation Purpose of Submittal: Update the Board of Trustees on the implementation of Workday at the University of Rhode Island.
Points to Consider: The University of Rhode Island launched its Workday implementation on January 12, 2026, to replace its PeopleSoft Human Resources and Finance systems and the PBCS budgeting platform.
The project has successfully completed the Planning stage and is currently in the Architect and Configure stage, where functional and technical teams are configuring business requirements, validating system design, and testing configurations to ensure alignment with institutional needs.
Overall, the implementation remains on track across the majority of workstreams and continues to perform within planned timeline and budget expectations.

Project leadership and governance have remained stable and effective, providing consistent oversight and decision-making throughout the implementation.
State system integration remains the most significant project risk.
Identified early in the implementation, this dependency continues to present challenges because critical aspects of the integration effort are outside the direct control of URI and rely on State of Rhode Island stakeholders and timelines.
URI and the State of Rhode Island leadership team have been meeting monthly on the project status.
Change management continues to be a key factor for the implementation.
Over the past several weeks, outreach and engagement efforts have increased to provide opportunities for faculty, staff, and campus stakeholders to learn about the Workday program.
These activities are focused on building awareness, preparing the University community for upcoming changes, and driving adoption to support a successful transition to the new system .
Overall, the project remains on track , however we are mindful and maintain focus on risk management, stakeholder engagement, and organizational readiness.

Review of Enacted State Budget Enclosure Abby Benson, Vice President, Administration and Finance The Finance and Facilities Committee reviewed the FY27 state budget approved by the General Assembly on June 9, 2026.
Vice President Abby Benson reported that the General Assembly approved a $4.2 million increase to the operating budget, an amount in line with the Governor’s Recommended Budget (GRB), but well below the University’s request of $37.6 million.
She reminded the Committee of the three categories for the request: Operating Budget Shortfall, Current Service Level, and Strategic Initiatives, of which only the Current Service Level was funded.
She noted that of the $4.2 million increase in the operating budget, $1.3 million of this amount reflects support for corresponding expenses imposed by the state for centralized services.
Strategic Initiatives have not been funded for a number of years, but the University continues to maintain this request to signal the importance of these initiatives.

Vice President Benson also noted that the University received $15.2 million for general asset protection, $1.6 million for a campus access control pilot program (to determine the system of record for access control at RI), $8.0 million in RICAP ADA project support and also $18.0 million in RICAP Building Envelope work.
The Capital Improvement Plan included a GO Bond request for $165.7 million for the Integrated Health Building, with the legislature supporting the project at $165.0 million.
The bill also included Kushner authorization for URI to issue revenue bonds for Repaving and Hardscaping ($20.0 million) and Automotive and Administrative Services ($14.4 million).
The enacted budget included $5.0 million for medical school startup funds (operating).
Additionally, the full-time equivalent (FTE) cap was increased by 200 with a new auxiliary cap of 450 FTEs, inclusive of the total FTE count.
Committee members had no questions on the approved budget. 3.

Creation of a College Liaison Special Committee
Effective starting spring 2027
The College Liaison Special Committee shall consist of ten senators, one from each college that elects Faculty Senators and one from the Library, who are referred to as the ‘Liaison’ from their unit to the Faculty Senate. If the Faculty Senate votes to approve creation of this Special Committee in fall 2026, senators from each college/Library will select one of their number to serve during the spring 2027 semester in the role of Liaison. Following senate elections in May 2027, senators from each college/Library will again select one of their number in August to serve during the 2027-2028 academic year in the role of Liaison. Liaisons may be re-elected but must be a current senator. The Senate President and FSEC will ask for volunteers to chair this committee on a one-year basis and identify a chair for vote by the Faculty Senate at its September meeting.

College Liaison Committee members are charged with ensuring that faculty in each college are informed of pertinent university-level matters and communicate senate- and college-level concerns in both directions. Liaisons attend all-college faculty meetings and will be given the opportunity to give a report on senate activities. The Liaison also attends meetings of the Faculty Senate in their role as a current senator.
Liaisons have two responsibilities in addition to attending college- and senate-level meetings. First, Liaisons provide a brief monthly update regarding senate/university-level matters to faculty in their college. Second, Liaisons represent their college on the College Liaison Committee. This committee meets at least once per semester to address issues requiring inter-college coordination. The College Liaison Committee is a Special Committee of the Faculty Senate, chaired by the Vice President of the Faculty Senate who serves as a non-voting member.

This contract represents ongoing support services which are part of the current operations of the campus for service and repair to the University’s chillers and HVAC systems.
The contract for these services has not yet been awarded, but is expected to be awarded by the State to begin July 1, 2026.
This proposed contract will replace the award previously approved by the Board in November 2023 for $6M over three years.
Because this proposed contract is in the bid award determination process , no supplier is identified at this time.

Once the State is ready to award the contract to the successful bidder, we anticipate that contract value to be closer to $5.0M, but we are requesting approval for a cap of $5.50M on the contract to allow for flexibility.
The targeted $5.0M expense is less than the prior contract for similar services because certain components of the contract have been updated and certain services split out to better serve the University.
Recommendation: It is recommended that the University of Rhode Island Board of Trustees approve the proposed award for the Chiller Maintenance and Repair contract, which is expected to be issued for July 1, 2026.
Points to Consider: This prior contract approved by the Board of Trustees in November of 2023 exceeded its original estimated value largely due to unanticipated emergency repairs and required equipment replacement.
To better assess the new contract, the Facilities Operations group completed a comprehensive review of the services provided and decided to split out certain components of the work to better foster competition.

To meet the HVAC and chiller maintenance and repair needs of the University th rough this new time and materials contract, the University is proposing a $5.50M cap to the spend that includes unanticipated emergencies.
The University’s Facilities Operations group continues to work with URI Purchasing to maximize contracting options for HVAC equipment replacement, as well as preventative maintenance and repair.
